page: Microsoft Azure FX32mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The instance is configured with 672.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD.

In benchmark testing, the FX32mds_v2 demonstrates strong memory and processing capabilities. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show read speeds of 232.79 GB/sec and write speeds of 136.78 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-core performance is notable, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reaches 200.05 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput is measured at 49.05 GB/sec. However, while small and medium model LLM prompt processing speeds are strong, large model text generation is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 2.72 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The hardware profile of this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, balancing high-frequency Intel Xeon processing with a substantial memory footprint and fast local NVMe storage. This makes the FX32mds_v2 highly efficient for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and data-intensive enterprise applications. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the built-in AMX instructions provide a viable alternative for CPU-based inference tasks.
